subject: math
title: Repeating and Increasing Patterns: Core, Shape Patterns and Number Patterns to 100
seo_title: Grade 2 Repeating and Increasing Patterns Worksheets: Free Math Practice with Answer Key (BC Curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 math worksheets on repeating and increasing patterns: find the core, extend increasing shape patterns, count by 2s, 5s and 10s to 100, fill in missing parts and make predictions. 100 questions with an answer key, matched to the BC curriculum.
key_big: Find what repeats or what changes each time.
key_sub: In a repeating pattern, find the core: the part that repeats. In an increasing pattern, find the jump and check it every time: 4, 7, 10 is “start at 4 and add 3 each time.”
body_html:
Repeating patterns and the core

A repeating pattern has a part that repeats again and again. That part is the core. Find the core, then say the pattern out loud to check it.

You can show the same pattern in a new way. Red, blue, blue can be clap, snap, snap or A, B, B.

Increasing shape patterns

An increasing pattern gets bigger each time. Count each figure. Then find how many are added each time.

Increasing number patterns to 100

Find the jump from one number to the next. Check that the same jump works every time.

Next number

14, 24, 34, ☐

The jump is +10. Only the tens digit goes up. 34 + 10 = 44.

Answer: 44

Missing number

60, ☐, 80, 90

The rule is add 10. 60 + 10 = 70. Check: 70 + 10 = 80.

Answer: 70

Predict

Beads go red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue … What colour is the 10th bead?

Red is at 1, 4, 7 and 10.

Answer: red

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Wrong core: red, blue, blue has the core “red, blue”Say it again and again to check: red, blue, blue
Using only the first step: 1, 3, 6 is “add 2”Check every jump: +2, +3, so the next jump is +4
Using the first number as the rule: 4, 7, 10 is “add 4”Find the jump: start at 4 and add 3 each time
Counting on 1: 20, 25, 30, 31Use the same jump each time: 20, 25, 30, 35
Mixing up the figure number and the number of objectsFigure 3 is the 3rd picture. Count what is in it

faq.q: What patterns do Grade 2 students learn in BC math?
faq.a: In the BC curriculum (Patterning), Grade 2 students make, describe and extend repeating patterns and increasing patterns. They find the core, find missing parts and make number patterns to 100 by 2s, 5s and 10s.

faq.q: What is the core of a repeating pattern?
faq.a: The core is the part of the pattern that repeats. In red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, the core is red, blue, blue.
An increasing pattern gets bigger by the same amount each time, like 4, 7, 10, 13. The rule is “start at 4 and add 3 each time.”

faq.q: How can I practise patterns with my child at home?
faq.a: Make patterns with beads, blocks or claps, and count coins by 2s, 5s and 10s with toonies, nickels and dimes. Ask what comes next and how they know.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is circle, square. It repeats again and again. So next comes square. A circle is always followed by a square.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is red, blue, blue. It repeats again and again. So next comes blue. After red come two blues. Then red again.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is triangle, circle, square. It repeats again and again. So next comes circle.

items.q: What is the core of this pattern?
items.e: The core is the part that repeats. Here it is circle, square. Then it starts again. “circle, square, circle” is too long. It goes into the next core.

items.q: Which letters show the same pattern?
c: A A B A A B
A B A B A B
A B C A B C
A B B A B B
items.e: Red is A. Blue is B. Red, blue, blue is A, B, B. So the pattern is A B B A B B.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What number comes next?
items.e: The core is 1, 2, 2. The row ends with 2, 2. So next comes 1. 3 counts on, but this is a repeating pattern.

items.q: What is the core of this pattern?
items.e: The core is the part that repeats. Here it is red, blue, blue. Then it starts again. “red, blue” is too short. After red come two blues.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is up, right, down, left. It repeats again and again. So next comes down. The arrow turns a quarter turn each time, like a clock.

items.q: Kai makes a sound pattern. What comes next?
items.e: The core is clap, stomp, stomp. It repeats again and again. So next comes stomp. There are two stomps in each core, not one.
The core is yellow, yellow, red, red. That is 4 shapes. 2 is the number of colours, not shapes.

c: A B B A A B B A
A A B A A B A A
A B A B A B A B
A A B B A A B B
items.e: Yellow is A. Red is B. Two yellow, two red: A, A, B, B. So it is A A B B A A B B.

items.q: What is the core of this pattern?
items.e: The core is the part that repeats. Here it is triangle, circle, square. Then it starts again. Check by saying it: triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle, square.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What comes next?
items.e: The core is blue square, blue square, red triangle. It repeats again and again. So next comes red triangle. Both the shape and the colour change. It is a red triangle.

items.q: Owen moves in a pattern: hop, hop, turn, hop, hop, turn. Which letters show the same pattern?
c: A B A B A B
A A B A A B
A A B B A A
A B B A B B
items.e: Hop is A. Turn is B. Hop, hop, turn is A, A, B. So it is A A B A A B.

items.q: Which pattern has the core A, B, B?
c: A B B A B B A B B
A A B A A B A A B
A B A B A B A B
A B B B A B B B
items.e: The core is one A and two Bs. Say it again and again: A B B A B B A B B.

items.q: Simran makes a pattern with the core square, circle, circle. She makes the core 3 times. How many circles does she use?
items.e: Each core has 2 circles. 3 cores: 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 circles. 3 counts only 1 circle in each core.

items.q: The pattern repeats. What are the next two shapes?
items.e: The core is blue square, blue square, red triangle. The row ends with a red triangle. So the core starts again: blue square, blue square.

items.q: Which of these is NOT a repeating pattern?
c: A A B A A B A A B
A B A A B B B A
A B A B A B A B
A B C A B C A B C
items.e: The others repeat the same core each time. A B A A B B B A has no part that repeats.

items.q: Jasleen makes a pattern: red, blue, blue. She makes one mistake. Which circle is wrong?
items.e: Red goes at 1, 4 and 7. Circles 5 and 6 should be blue. Circle 5 is red, so it is the mistake.

items.q: Hana makes a pattern with blocks: red, red, blue. She wants to show the same pattern with sounds. Which one works?
items.e: Red, red, blue is A, A, B. Clap, clap, snap is also A, A, B. So clap, clap, snap works.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many cubes are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 2, 3, 4. Each figure has 1 more cube. 4 + 1 = 5 cubes. 4 is Figure 3 again. 6 adds 2, not 1.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 2, 4, 6. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 6 + 2 = 8 tiles. 7 counts on 1, not 2.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 5 + 2 = 7 tiles. 6 counts on 1, not 2.

items.q: What kind of pattern is this?
items.e: Count: 5, 10, 15. Each figure has more dots. It is an increasing pattern.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many dots are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 5, 10, 15. Each figure has 5 more dots. 15 + 5 = 20 dots. 16 counts on 1, not 5.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 15 cubes?
items.e: Keep going: 6, 9, 12, 15. Figure 4 has 15 cubes. 15 is the number of cubes, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 3, 5, 7. Each figure has 2 more sticks. 7 + 2 = 9 sticks. Count the sticks, not the triangles.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many dots are in Figure 5?
items.e: Keep adding 5: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25. Figure 5 has 25 dots. 20 is Figure 4. 21 counts on 1, not 5.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many cubes are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 6, 9, 12. Each figure has 3 more cubes. 12 + 3 = 15 cubes. Each new tower has 3 cubes.

items.q: How many sticks are added each time?
items.e: Count: 4, 7, 10. 4 + 3 = 7 and 7 + 3 = 10. 3 sticks are added each time. 4 is how many sticks Figure 1 has. It is not the jump.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many chairs are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count each figure: 4, 6, 8. Each figure has 2 more chairs. 8 + 2 = 10 chairs. 16 gives each table 4 chairs. But no chairs fit where the tables touch.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 30 dots?
items.e: Keep going: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. Figure 6 has 30 dots. 30 is the number of dots, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 12 tiles?
items.e: Keep going: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12. Figure 6 has 12 tiles. 12 is the number of tiles, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many cubes are in Figure 5?
items.e: Keep adding 1: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6. Figure 5 has 6 cubes. 5 is the figure number. Each tower has 1 more cube than its figure number.

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of tiles?
items.e: Figure 1 has 1 tile. Count each figure: 1, 3, 5. The rule is start at 1 and add 2 each time.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. Which figure has 9 tiles?
items.e: Keep going: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Figure 5 has 9 tiles. 9 is the number of tiles, not the figure number.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 5?
items.e: Keep adding 2: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. Figure 5 has 11 sticks. 15 counts 3 sticks for each triangle. But the triangles share sticks.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many tiles are in Figure 4?
items.e: Count: 1, 3, 6. The jumps are +2, then +3. Each jump is 1 more, so the next jump is +4. 6 + 4 = 10. 8 uses only the first step (+2).

items.q: What is the pattern rule for the number of sticks?
items.e: Figure 1 has 4 sticks. Count each figure: 4, 7, 10. The rule is start at 4 and add 3 each time. 4 is how many sticks Figure 1 has. It is not the jump.

items.q: The pattern keeps going. How many sticks are in Figure 6?
items.e: Keep adding 3: 4, 7, 10, 13, 16, 19. Figure 6 has 19 sticks. 24 counts 4 sticks for each square. But the squares share sticks.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 16 + 2 = 18. 17 is only 1 more.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 35 + 5 = 40. 36 is only 1 more.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 40 + 2 = 42. 41 is only 1 more.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 70 + 10 = 80. 71 is only 1 more. 90 jumps 20, not 10.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
items.e: 35 + 5 = 40. Every jump is the same. The rule is add 5 each time. The numbers go up, so the rule adds.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 34 + 10 = 44. The ones digit stays 4. Only the tens digit goes up.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 5 more. 65 + 5 = 70. Counting by 5s, the numbers end in 5 or 0.

items.q: Start at 30. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +5. Count on by 5s from 30: 35, 40, 45, 50. You land on 50.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
items.e: 62 + 10 = 72. Every jump is the same. The rule is add 10 each time. The numbers go up, so the rule adds.

items.q: The shaded squares count by 2s. What is the next shaded number?
items.e: 12 + 2 = 14. Shade every second square.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 10 more. 43 + 10 = 53. With +10, the ones digit stays 3. 44 changes the ones digit.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
items.e: 3 + 5 = 8. Every jump is the same. The rule is add 5 each time. 3 is the first number, not the jump.

items.q: This is part of a hundreds chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: The number just above is 10 less. So the ? is 10 more than 34. 34 + 10 = 44.

items.q: What number comes next?
items.e: Each number is 2 more. 72 + 2 = 74. 73 is only 1 more. 82 adds 10, not 2.

items.q: The shaded squares count by 10s. What is the next shaded number?
items.e: 24 + 10 = 34. By 10s, go straight down one row. The ones digit stays 4.

items.q: What is the pattern rule?
items.e: 41 + 2 = 43. Every jump is the same. The rule is add 2 each time. The numbers are odd. Counting by 2s from an odd number gives odd numbers.

items.q: Start at 65. Make the jumps. Where do you land?
items.e: Each jump is +10. Count on by 10s from 65: 75, 85, 95. You land on 95.

items.q: This is part of a hundreds chart. What number goes in the box with the ?
items.e: The number just below is 10 more. So the ? is 10 less than 68. 68 − 10 = 58.

items.q: Ryan counts by 5s from 0: 0, 5, 10, 15 … Which number will he say?
items.e: Counting by 5s from 0, every number ends in 5 or 0. Only 45 ends that way.

items.q: Nadia counts by 10s from 6: 6, 16, 26 … Which number will she say?
items.e: Counting by 10s from 6, every number ends in 6. Only 56 ends in 6. 60 and 50 are what you say counting by 10s from 0.

items.q: What is missing from this pattern?
items.e: The core is circle, square. Say the pattern from the start: circle, square, circle, square, circle. The missing one is circle.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 10 each time. 40 + 10 = 50. Check: 50 + 10 = 60.

items.q: What is missing from this pattern?
items.e: The core is red, blue, blue. Say the pattern from the start: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue. The missing one is blue.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 5 each time. 20 + 5 = 25. Check: 25 + 5 = 30.

items.q: What is missing from this pattern?
items.e: The core is triangle, circle, square. Say the pattern from the start: triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle, square, triangle, circle. The missing one is circle.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 10 each time. 60 + 10 = 70. Check: 70 + 10 = 80.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 2 each time. Go back one step from 14: 14 − 2 = 12. The first number is 2 less than 14.

items.q: What is missing from this pattern?
items.e: The core is up, right, down, left. Say the pattern from the start: up, right, down, left, up, right. The missing one is right.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 2 each time. 48 + 2 = 50. Check: 50 + 2 = 52.

items.q: What is missing from this pattern?
items.e: The core is blue square, blue square, red triangle. Say the pattern from the start: blue square, blue square, red triangle. The missing one is red triangle.

items.q: Figure 2 is hidden. How many tiles are in Figure 2?
items.e: Figure 1 has 1 tile. Figure 3 has 5 tiles. The pattern goes up by the same amount each time: 1, 3, 5. The rule is add 2.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 5 each time. 75 + 5 = 80. Check: 80 + 5 = 85.

items.q: Which two numbers are missing, in order?
items.e: The rule is add 5 each time. Fill in each box: 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. The missing numbers are 15, 25.

items.q: What number is missing?
items.e: The rule is add 10 each time. 38 + 10 = 48. Check: 48 + 10 = 58.

items.q: Figure 3 is hidden. How many tiles are in Figure 3?
items.e: Count: 2, 4, ?, 8. Each figure has 2 more tiles. 4 + 2 = 6. Check: 6 + 2 = 8. 3 is the figure number.

items.q: Which two numbers are missing, in order?
items.e: The rule is add 2 each time. Fill in each box: 22, 24, 26, 28, 30. The missing numbers are 24, 28.

items.q: One number in this pattern is wrong. Which one?
items.e: The rule is add 10: 20, 30, 40, 50, 60. 45 should be 50.

items.q: Figure 1 is not shown. How many sticks are in Figure 1?
items.e: Count: Figure 2 has 7, Figure 3 has 10, Figure 4 has 13. Each figure adds 3 sticks. Go back one step: 7 − 3 = 4.

items.q: Liam counts by 5s: 35, 40, 45, 49, 55. One number is a mistake. What should it be?
What number is missing?
items.e: The jumps are +2, +3, then +4, then +5. 6 + 4 = 10. Check: 10 + 5 = 15. 8 uses only the first step (+2).

items.q: Olivia counts nickels by 5s. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 5s: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30¢. 6¢ counts the coins, not the cents.

items.q: Ethan strings beads in this pattern. He keeps going. What colour is the 10th bead?
items.e: The core has 3 beads. Keep the pattern going and count. Red beads are at 1, 4, 7, 10. So the 10th bead is red.

items.q: A pair of mitts has 2 mitts. How many mitts are in 8 pairs?
items.e: Count by 2s 8 times: 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16. 8 is the number of pairs.

items.q: Kai counts dimes by 10s. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 10s: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60, 70¢. 7¢ counts the coins, not the cents.

items.q: Nadia lays out blocks in this pattern. She keeps going. What shape is the 11th block?
items.e: The core has 2 blocks. Keep the pattern going and count. Circles are at 1, 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. So the 11th block is a circle.

items.q: Ava gets 10 stickers each day. How many stickers does she have after 5 days?
items.e: Count by 10s 5 times: 10, 20, 30, 40, 50. 15 adds 10 and 5.

items.q: Chloe counts toonies by 2s. A toonie is $2. How much money is this?
items.e: Count by 2s: 2, 4, 6, 8, $10. $5 counts the coins, not the dollars.

items.q: Emma skates at the rink in Kamloops. She skates 2 laps on Monday, 4 laps on Tuesday and 6 laps on Wednesday. The pattern keeps going. How many laps does she skate on Friday?
items.e: Add 2 each day: Thursday 8, Friday 10. 8 is Thursday.
The core has 4 stars. Keep the pattern going and count. Yellow stars are at 2, 6, 10. So the 10th star is yellow.

items.q: 7 students each hold up one hand. Count the fingers by 5s. How many fingers are there?
items.e: Count by 5s 7 times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35. 12 adds 7 and 5.

items.q: Owen has 10 loonies in his piggy bank. He adds 5 loonies each week. How many loonies are there after 4 weeks?
items.e: Start at 10 and add 5 each week: 15, 20, 25, 30. 20 forgets the 10 loonies he started with.

items.q: A sunflower is 20 cm tall. It grows 10 cm each week. How tall is it after 3 weeks?
items.e: Add 10 each week: 30, 40, 50 cm. 30 is only 1 week. 23 adds 1 each week, not 10.

items.q: Each canoe on the lake has 2 paddles. How many paddles are in 9 canoes?
The class library in Surrey has 20 books. Each week, students bring 5 more books. How many books are there after 4 weeks?
items.e: Add 5 each week: 25, 30, 35, 40. 35 is after 3 weeks. 24 adds 1 each week. 9 adds 4 and 5.

items.q: Sofia has gym class every Tuesday. The first three are on November 3, November 10 and November 17. When is the next one?
items.e: There are 7 days in a week. Add 7 each time: 3, 10, 17, 24. November 18 is only the next day. November 27 adds 10, not 7.

items.q: Leah plants tulips in this pattern: red, red, yellow, red, red, yellow … She plants 12 tulips. How many are yellow?
items.e: The core red, red, yellow has 3 tulips. 12 tulips make 4 cores: 3, 6, 9, 12. Each core has 1 yellow, so 4 are yellow. 8 is the number of red tulips.

items.q: A quilt has a row of squares in this pattern. The row has 15 squares. How many are green?
items.e: The core is yellow, green, green. 15 squares make 5 cores: 3, 6, 9, 12, 15. Each core has 2 green, so 2, 4, 6, 8, 10. 5 counts only 1 green in each core.

items.q: Mateo counts by 10s from 0. He says, “I will say 75.” Is he right?
c: No. He says numbers that end in 0.
items.e: Counting by 10s from 0: 10, 20, 30 … 70, 80. Every number ends in 0. 75 ends in 5, so he is not right.

items.q: Zara builds towers. Tower 1 has 3 blocks. Tower 2 has 5 blocks. Tower 3 has 7 blocks. How many blocks are in Tower 6?
items.e: Add 2 each time: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, 13. 18 uses 3 as the jump, but 3 is only Tower 1. 11 is Tower 5.

items.q: A Grade 2 class collects money for the Terry Fox Run. They have $15 after week 1, $25 after week 2 and $35 after week 3. The pattern keeps going. How much do they have after week 5?
items.e: Add $10 each week: $15, $25, $35, $45, $55. $45 is week 4. $75 adds $15 each week, but $15 is only where they started.
